project.name: Witness
project.pitch: A human-in-the-loop decision desk that screens benefits applications with grounded AI and requires a named officer to decide.
project.problem: Public benefits screening is high-volume and high-stakes, yet fully automated scoring puts the cost of error on the applicant: a wrong denial has no owner and no reviewable basis. Witness keeps the model advisory, makes every rule deterministic, and makes a named officer accountable for every final decision.
project.human: The human is a structural stage, not a reviewer bolted on afterwards. The automated pipeline can reach Verified or Needs review; it has no code path that produces a denial. A final decision requires an officer name and a written reason, which are appended to a hash-chained ledger. When evidence is missing, contradictory or uncited, the verifier abstains and escalates the case instead of guessing. The model may only make the outcome more cautious, never less.
project.built_with: Python and FastAPI, deployed on Alternate Clouds from a public GitHub repository. Fact extraction uses Groq's llama-3.3-70b-versatile with verbatim-quote grounding; if the model is unavailable it falls back to a deterministic label reader. Policy is evaluated by a deterministic seven-clause rules engine in code. PDF text extraction uses pypdf. The audit ledger is an append-only SHA-256 hash chain in SQLite. No n8n workflow; no MCP servers.
